Step: PLAN SPLIT (round 1). Propose the first split of the property: where does the hardness come from (which index, pointer or slot does the proof quantify over)? Each piece is first checked with a 3 s cap, 8 pieces at a time; pieces that time out come back to you with timings.

Signals:
srFull  width 1  wire
srEmpty  width 1  wire
srDataOut  width 4  wire
rst  width 1  input
rbFull  width 1  wire
rbEmpty  width 1  wire
rbDataOut  width 4  wire
push  width 1  input
pop  width 1  input
equal  width 1  wire
dataIn  width 4  input
bb_first  width 1  register
sr_dataOut  width 4  wire
sr_empty  width 1  register
sr_full  width 1  wire
sr_tail  width 4  register
rb_dataOut  width 4  wire
rb_empty  width 1  register
rb_full  width 1  wire
rb_head  width 4  register
rb_tail  width 4  register
prop_a  width 1  wire
prop_en  width 1  wire
sr_mem_0 .. sr_mem_15 and rb_mem_0 .. rb_mem_15: registers, width 4 (the FIFO storage)

Answer: {"split":<explicit cases or index direction>,"reason":"..."}

raw_response: {"split":{"index":"rb_tail","bits":4,"auto":true},"reason":"The property relates the two FIFO stores through a rotational offset: slot j of the shift-register FIFO (sr_mem_j) must hold the same word as rb_mem[(rb_tail+j) mod 16], and the flag correspondence (sr_tail vs rb_head/rb_tail, full/empty) depends on the same offset. The hardness is the proof quantifying over this modular index alignment over 16 slots; fixing rb_tail pins down which sr/rb memory pair is being compared and turns the modular index arithmetic into a fixed permutation. Splitting rb_tail top-bit-first (auto) instantiates the offset incrementally; residual cases that still quantify over sr_tail/rb_head and individual slots are left for later rounds."}
